title: Cross-architecture steady-state load harness and normalized cost-per-token dashboard
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: Build a repeatable, automated load-testing harness that measures steady-state tokens/sec and p95 latency across a hardware matrix (A10, L4, A100, H100), computes a normalized cost-per-token metric, and feeds a regression detector that alerts on production-impacting degradations. This ticket covers harness design, benchmark datasets, warmup/priming strategy for KV-cache workloads, aggregation logic, dashboard wiring, and alert thresholds. The output will be a stored dataset per run (S3), a Grafana dashboard with normalized cost and p95 heatmaps, and an automated GitHub Action that runs the matrix nightly and after PRs to runtime changes.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run the full matrix (A10/L4/A100/H100) end-to-end without manual intervention
For each run we persist: median tokens/sec, mean tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, error rate, tail-kv-hit ratio, and raw token counts
Normalized cost-per-token is calculated using committed GPU-hour pricing + amortized infra for each region and is visible in dashboard
Regression detector raises a PR or issue when tokens/sec drops >10% relative to baseline or p95 increases >5% on stable model variants
Nightly matrix runs and post-runtime-merge runs produce artifacts in S3 and link to a summary GitHub issue
On-alert runbook created and validated by SRE and runtime owners
test_plan: Synthetic workloads: 3 prompt families: short-chat (16-64 tokens), instruct (64-256 tokens), long-context (512-2048 tokens). Use deterministic seeds and common tokenization to ensure cross-arch comparability
Workload pattern: steady open-loop arrival until steady-state (5 minute warmup) then 30 minute steady run per node config. Repeat 3 trials and aggregate medians
KV-cache priming: run priming phase with 100 unique prefixes to warm KV and measure cold-vs-warm delta
Concurrency sweep: run at target QPS levels mapped to 50%, 75%, 95% line-rate for each GPU type to capture throughput curves
Failure injection: intermittent network 50ms added on one trial to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies
Cost calculation: use commit prices (contracted GPU $/hour) + infra overhead (storage, load-gen hosts) normalized to cost-per-token and to Cost Efficiency Index (CEI) = tokens/sec per $1hr
runbook: If regression alert fires: gather last 3 nightly runs artifacts from s3://redwood-bench/hw-matrix/ENG-27655
Compare raw logs and profiling traces (nvprof/pmu) between baseline and current run
If tokens/sec dropped >10%: verify kernel selection and quantization flags in model shard config
If p95 increased >5%: check queuing (CPU), batching pipeline backpressure, and KV-cache miss amplification
Open a triage issue with runtime-1.22 label and assign to serving-runtime owners
Rollback plan: pin traffic to previous runtime release or fallback model variant if degradation persists
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spec drafted after sync with PM and SRE. Chose 3 synthetic prompt families to cover typical production distributions.
2026-02-18: Decided on 5 minute warmup + 30 minute steady run to reduce noise; validated with quick A100 pilot.
2026-02-28: Implemented baseline cost normalization algorithm (commit prices + infra amortization). Added CEI metric. PR opened: bench-harness#422.

2026-03-04: Nightly job added to GitHub Actions; first full matrix run completed for A100/H100. Observed unexpected 12% tokens/sec variance on L4 in region eu-west-1; created ENG-27901 to investigate GPU driver/AMI mismatch.

2026-03-10: Regression detector added (EWMA + percentile shift test). Thresholds tuned: tokens/sec drop >10% or p95 >5% -> create issue with triage tag. SRE reviewed runbook and signed off on alerting steps.
release_notes: Adds automated cross-architecture steady-state harness, nightly matrix runs, and a normalized cost-per-token dashboard. Includes regression detection rules and starter runbook for triage. Will enable more confident runtime changes and cost-forecasting for upcoming Dedicated SKU pricing experiments.
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the cost normalization assumptions: we use committed GPU/hr for each instance family and amortize ephemeral infra at 10% of GPU cost. If finance wants different allocation, update bench-harness/config/costs.yaml. Also validate warmup length for L4; early trials showed longer priming than A100 due to smaller on-device cache.
